title: Real Portraits Replace a Crowned Emoji in History Lessons | vitalii.no
description:
Boytasks' first history cards used word tiles and a crowned emoji to stand in for a king, so a child had to read an abstract label instead of recognizing who the event was actually about from a real picture. Geometry had no model effect of its own either — area and perimeter were taught only as text and numbers, with no rectangle a child could see built from counted squares.

I added two effects to the lesson-video model kit: one shows an essence picture and sentence, then 3 to 6 chapters — each a real portrait or painting the camera slowly pushes into, a dated stage pill, the person's name, and one plain sentence — before a recap tiles every chapter together. The other, built in Remotion, draws a rectangle on squared paper, fills it row by row with unit squares while a counter climbs to the product, walks a marker around the perimeter summing each side, then folds a triangle's outside pieces onto its inside half to show why a triangle is half its rectangle.

A history topic now plays out as a chain of real faces and places a child can recognize at a glance, stage by stage, and a rectangle's area is no longer a formula to memorize: the child watches 7 by 4 squares actually counted to 28 square meters before the number appears.
